score.about: ChatGPT now lets businesses claim listings, but claiming means agreeing its AI may call you and you give up some legal claims; here are four steps, and it's only for existing US listings.
score.gets: Something to do plus a heads-up: the four claim steps and the address, and that claiming signs you up for AI calls and a covenant not to sue. Mildly useful.
score.stop: Barely. The first 3 seconds are a waving cartoon at a desk and a small white card; the stronger line, 'OpenAI's AI may call you', lands at 3 to 6 s.
score.leave_at: about 22 to 27 s: the scary part is defused fast, then it is a slow how-to with the same figure, desk and arm in every frame
score.confused: 'Covenant Not to Sue' and 'certain claims' with no plain meaning; 'You can opt out here.' is a link nobody can tap; the address clipping is cut at its right edge; 'read the terms, then decide' gives no verdict; 'whoever runs your Google listing' came from nowhere
score.comment: Maybe one skeptical line: 'So I sign away my right to sue to get a free listing? Pass.'
